# Plan: local deploy — render a whole system's manifests for a local cluster

> Revision 3. Revision 1 was reviewed against the codebase (verdict:
> rework); revision 2 resolved its five required items and was re-reviewed
> (verdict: approve-with-changes). This revision applies the re-review's
> five amendments: the catalog carrier (was silently dropped by
> `rawSpec`), the FetchLibrary test seams on `LocalOptions`, the pinned
> image-reference shape, values layering, and the pinnable predicate.

## The problem

The testing ladder has a gap at the top:

| Level | Scope | External systems |
|---|---|---|
| unit | one block | mocked in-process |
| integration | the pipeline in one component | mocked/stubbed |
| host | components together | mocked or in-memory |
| **local deploy** | **everything, deployed on a local cluster** | **real protocol, fake peer** |

Today nothing produces deployable manifests for a local cluster. The GitOps
machinery (`deploy init`, `deploy pin`, `deploy sync`) targets customer
environments through ArgoCD and is deliberately kubectl-free. A developer
who wants to run the full system locally — Dapr sidecars, pub/sub, bindings,
CronJob cadence and all — has to hand-write manifests.

The experience we want:

```
intropy int local <system> | kubectl apply -f -
```

One command, manifests on stdout, nothing written except one small state
file.

## The boundary

Three owners, no overlap:

| Owner | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| k3s setup scripts | The cluster, Dapr installation, and the fixture servers (sftp, smb, http stub) — **always installed**, at stable addresses with conventional dev credentials |
| intropy-templates repo | A `local` overlay on `deploy-host` / `deploy-component`, including the **closed fixture catalog**: one Dapr binding Component per fixture type, pointing at the conventional cluster addresses |
| this CLI | Reads the topology, asks one question per connector, renders into a temp dir, builds, streams YAML to stdout |

Consequences of "fixtures are always installed":

- The render is **unconditional**. The CLI never emits fixture servers at
  all, so there is no "include the sftp server only if some connector chose
  sftp" logic.
- Switching a connector's fidelity level (`file` → `sftp`) is a one-line
  edit in the state file and a re-apply. The cluster never changes.
- The CLI knows nothing about k3s. The emitted manifests are generic and
  would apply to any cluster with Dapr and the fixtures installed.

The fixture catalog is **closed**: `sftp`, `smb`, `http`, `file`. A system
needing something exotic hand-writes that Component in its own repo until
the pattern proves common enough to promote into the catalog (a template
PR, not a CLI release).

## The one coupling

The fixture contract — namespace, service names, ports, credentials — is
shared between the k3s scripts (which install the servers) and the
template's `local` overlay (which renders bindings pointing at them). One
doc, referenced from both repos. This is the only coupling between the two.

Conventions (initial proposal, finalized in that doc):

- namespace `fixtures`
- `sftp.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:22`, user/pass `intropy`/`intropy`
- `smb.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:445`
- `http.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:8080` (wiremock-style stub)

## The verb: `int local` — decided

Review finding 2 required deciding the verb in AGENTS.md terms instead of
deferring it. Decision: **`local`**, a new verb under `int`.

The AGENTS.md taxonomy rule: "New verbs need a reason that the set above
cannot express, and the reason goes in this file with the verb, not in a
commit message." The reason, to be added to the taxonomy with the verb:

> **`local`** renders a system's deployable manifests for the local
> development cluster to stdout, for piping to kubectl. `create` scaffolds
> project source on disk; `init` scaffolds a GitOps tree and pushes a
> branch. Neither emits a render to a stream, and both the GitOps `deploy`
> family is excluded by its own contract ("all through the GitOps
> repository and ArgoCD, never kubectl" — `deploy.go`).

Why not the alternatives:

- `int show <system> --manifests`: the command prompts, writes workspace
  state, and renders backing configuration — more than "prints the details
  of exactly one thing". `show` stays honest.
- A `deploy` subcommand: excluded by `deploy`'s documented contract, and
  by the parent command's design note that no component name may be
  shadowed by a subcommand.
- `int create local <system>`: collides with the template positional arg.
- `deploy-local` (rev 1's name): a hyphenated compound unlike every
  existing verb; nothing in the taxonomy licenses compounds.

## The local facts model — no GitOps repo involved

Review findings 3 and 4: `deploy init`'s facts all derive from a GitOps
checkout (`openSession`, `deploy.yaml`, `resolveInitDomain`). None of that
exists in this flow. This section specifies what replaces `newInitFacts`
— the plan's largest addition over rev 1.

`localFacts` (new, in `internal/deploy/local.go`):

| initFacts field | Source in `deploy init` | Source in `localFacts` |
|---|---|---|
| `Domain` | GitOps tree / workspace layout / `--domain` | **Omitted from staged paths entirely** (see below) |
| `System` | topology / `--system` | Same: topology record, `--system` override |
| `Environments` | `selectEnvironments(deploy.yaml)` | Constant: `["local"]` |
| `Registry` | `deploy.yaml` | Constant `"dev"` — placeholder only; every Deployment image is set by the CLI's kustomize `images[]` override (see `--image`), so the rendered registry is never pulled from |
| `AppNamespace` | `deploy.yaml` argocd section | Empty — ArgoCD facts have no local meaning |
| `Platform` | `deploy.yaml` platform section | Constants: provider `kubernetes`, pubsub `redis`, secretStore `kubernetes` — matching what the k3s scripts install |
| `Model` / `Scaffolds` / `Selected` | topology + scaffold walk | Same — unchanged reuse of `newInitModel`, `matchScaffolds`, `selectComponents` |

### Staged layout: flat, no domain segment

`deploy init` stages into `domains/<domain>/<system>/<component>/` because
staged paths must be repo-relative for the commit. `int local` has no repo,
so the staging tree is flat:

```
<tmp>/
  kustomization.yaml          <- written by the CLI (below)
  host/                       <- deploy-host rendered once, env=local
    overlays/local/...
  <component>/                <- deploy-component per component
    overlays/local/...
```

`componentRelPath` is not reused; a `localRelPath(system, component)` =
`<component>` keeps paths stable without inventing a domain. (The system
segment is dropped too: the temp root already holds exactly one system.)

### The `.gitops` reserved map

Templates read `{{ .gitops.* }}` (reserved.go). For a local render the CLI
synthesizes:

```go
map[string]any{
    "domain":             "",          // no domain in a local render
    "system":             f.System,
    "component":          component,
    "env":                "local",
    "host":               HostDirName,
    "registry":           "dev",
    "argocdAppNamespace": "",
    "environments":       []string{"local"},
    "platform": map[string]any{
        "provider":    "kubernetes",
        "pubsub":      "redis",
        "secretStore": "kubernetes",
    },
}
```

Contract with the templates repo (stated in the fixture-contract doc): the
`local` overlay's skeleton files must not reference `.gitops` fields that
are empty locally — `argocdAppNamespace`, `domain`, `registry` outside base
image refs. Base files (rendered identically across envs per
`mergeRendered`) may reference `registry` freely because the CLI overrides
every image at build time.

### The root kustomization — CLI-written

Review finding 3: `deploy init` never builds the staging root (ArgoCD
builds each overlay separately), so nothing renders a root kustomization.
`int local` needs exactly one build, so the CLI writes it after rendering:

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: <--namespace value, default: system name>
resources:
  - host/overlays/local
  - <component>/overlays/local
  # ... one per selected component
images:
  - name: <image name as rendered by the component template>
    newName: <component>
    newTag: dev
  # ... one per pinnable component
```

- `namespace:` sets the target namespace on every resource — this is how
  `--namespace` is implemented; templates render namespace-agnostic.
- `images:` is how the conventional image tag is applied without the
  templates hardcoding it. **The rendered reference shape is pinned**
  (re-review finding 3): component templates render
  `image: <component>` — a bare name, no registry prefix, no tag. The
  fixture-contract doc states this, and the templates' unit tests assert
  it. The CLI therefore derives each `images[].name` as exactly the
  component name, and sets `newTag: dev` (no `newName`): the local image
  *is* `<component>:dev`, built and loaded by the scripts under that
  name. Pinning matters because kustomize image overrides match on the
  exact rendered name and **silently ignore unmatched entries** — a
  drifted convention would ship unoverridden images with no error. As a
  belt-and-braces check, `Local` parses the built output and errors if
  any Deployment image lacks a tag (catches template drift at render
  time rather than at pull time).
- **Pinnable predicate** (re-review finding 5): `images[]` gets one
  entry per selected component **except** the host — the same fact
  `requirePinnable` already encodes (`gitops.KindShared` has no image;
  init.go's HostDirName comment). The host renders no Deployment and no
  images entry.
- **`--image` grammar** (re-review finding 5): two forms, repeatable.
  `--image <component>=<name:tag>` overrides one component's entry
  (`newName` + `newTag`). `--image :<tag>` (a leading colon, no
  component) sets `newTag` on *every* pinnable component — the SemVer
  `-rc` flow (`--image :1.4.0-rc.3`). Any other shape is a usage error
  showing both forms.

### The build call

Review finding 1: the wrapper exists and the options struct must support
it. `internal/kustomize.Client.Build(ctx, dir)` (editor.go) runs
`kustomize build` and returns the stream; `plan.go` is the existing
caller. Accordingly:

```go
type LocalOptions struct {
    System      string
    SourceDir   string          // workspace root override (see below)
    Namespace   string
    Images      []string        // --image, repeatable (see below for the grammar)
    NoInput     bool
    TemplateVersion string      // same meaning as on deploy init
    TopologyFile string         // test seam, mirrors InitOptions.TopologyFile
    Runner      command.Runner  // for kustomize.Client; defaulted like InitOptions.applyDefaults

    // Library selection and fetch seams — mirrored from InitOptions
    // (init.go:104–114). GitHubBaseURL is how unit tests stub the
    // library fetch, exactly as init_test.go does; without it only the
    // INTROPY_TEMPLATES_DIR integration path could run. (Re-review
    // finding 2.)
    UserAgent     string
    Owner         string
    Repo          string
    GitHubBaseURL string
    HTTP          *http.Client

    Stdin       io.Reader
    Stdout      io.Writer
    Stderr      io.Writer
}

func Local(ctx context.Context, opts LocalOptions) error
```

`Runner` is required to construct `kustomize.Client`; `ctx` threads to
`Build`, `FetchLibrary`, and `runGraph`. The rendered YAML is written to
`opts.Stdout` — nothing else.

## The command

```
intropy int local <system> [--namespace <ns>] [--image <c>=<name:tag>]... [--template-version <tag>] [--no-input]
```

Behavior:

1. Resolve the workspace root (see below), run the host `graph` verb,
   decode via `topology.Decode` — same machinery as `deploy init`
   (`selectHost`, `discoverTopology`).
2. Load `.intropy/local.yaml`; prompt for unbound connectors; write the
   file back only if answers changed.
3. `template.FetchLibrary` (+ `defer lib.Close()`), render `deploy-host`
   once and `deploy-component` per component with env=`local` into
   `os.MkdirTemp`, `defer os.RemoveAll` on every exit path.
4. Write the root kustomization (above) into the staging root.
5. `kustomize.Client.Build(ctx, stagingRoot)`; write the multi-doc YAML
   to stdout.
6. Progress and hints to stderr only, house voice
   (`rendering order-extract for local`); follow-up hints in backticks on
   their own line.

`kustomize build` treats a temp dir identically to any other path; the
pipe to `kubectl apply -f -` sees only stdin. Two constraints, both
naturally satisfied:

- The staged tree is self-contained (kustomize's load restrictor refuses
  paths escaping the kustomization root) — the CLI renders everything into
  the temp root.
- No `helmCharts:` with remote repos in the templates — fixtures are
  pre-installed by the scripts, not rendered.

Flags:

- `--namespace` — target namespace in the emitted manifests (default: the
  system name). New flag, hand-written description.
- `--image` — repeatable image override (see root kustomization). New
  flag, hand-written description.
- `--template-version` — pins the template library release, same constant
  as `deploy init` (`flagUsageTemplateVer`). Review finding 8: rev 1
  omitted it; local renders must be able to pin the same library release
  the GitOps tree was scaffolded from.
- `--no-input` — fail instead of prompting (CI). Review finding 8: it
  already exists on two commands with two hand-written strings — this work
  introduces the shared `flagUsageNoInput` constant in `flagtext.go` and
  converts all three commands.
- No `--env` (always `local`), no `--output` (stdout is the manifest
  stream, period — review finding 8), no `--wait`, nothing that smells
  like kubectl.

Errors front-load what failed, remediation on a second line, per house
style — e.g. an unbound connector under `--no-input`:

```
connector erp-orders has no local binding in .intropy/local.yaml
run 'intropy int local <system>' interactively, or add it to the file
```

## What gets rendered — and what does not

Review finding 5: `deploy init`'s component template emits `component.yaml`
— repo metadata the rest of `deploy` reads, not a Kubernetes manifest.
Emitting it into a kubectl stream would be wrong.

The component template declares it in `spec.files`, so the mechanism is
already there: `int local` renders with a **narrowed file-rules filter**
that excludes `component.yaml` (and any future `*.md`/repo-metadata files
the contract doc enumerates). `renderOne` is reused with the filter
applied; the GitOps path is untouched. The exclusion list is part of the
fixture-contract doc so template authors know which files are repo-only.

ApplicationSet safety (the other half of finding 5): the guard lives in
the templates repo, not here. The ApplicationSet's cluster generator only
matches clusters registered in ArgoCD, so an `overlays/local/` directory
copied into a GitOps repo resolves to no cluster and generates no
Application. The templates-repo work item below includes verifying this
against the actual ApplicationSet template; this plan asserts no mechanism
of its own.

## Where the binding decision comes from

`internal/topology` is explicit: a `Connector` carries only its name,
external system, and directions. *"The deployed Dapr binding type, address,
and credentials are environment-owned deployment configuration, never part
of the record."* In production that decision lives in GitOps overlays. For
the local environment it lives nowhere — so `int local` is where it is
made.

The command asks **one question per connector** (not per component — the
topology's `UsedBy` already dedupes): "connector `erp-orders` (external
system `ERP`) — which binding?"

### The prompt: a new select prompter

Review finding 6: `template.AutoPrompter` is a missing-value text prompter;
no menu prompter exists. This work adds `template.SelectPrompter(stdin,
stderr, noInput)` to `internal/template/prompt.go` — shared, because a
catalog-driven menu is generally useful (skills flows are a likely second
caller). It presents a numbered menu, reads a number or name, and under
`--no-input` returns nil so the caller produces the two-line error above.

### The catalog: read from the fetched library, via a real Spec field

Review finding 6: a CLI-embedded catalog drifts from the templates repo
across releases. Decision: the catalog is **declared in the template
library** — a `fixtures` list in the `deploy-component` template's
`template.yaml`:

```yaml
spec:
  local:
    fixtures: [sftp, smb, http, file]
```

The CLI reads it from the fetched `lib` after `FetchLibrary`, so the
menu, the validation, and the rendered binding skeletons all come from
one release of one repo. Validation of `local.yaml` values happens
against the fetched catalog; an unknown value is a usage error naming
the valid ones. (Downgrade hazard noted in the first review is real but
bounded: the error message names exactly what the pinned library
supports, and `--template-version` is the escape hatch.)

**The carrier requires a manifest.go change** (re-review finding 1):
`Spec.UnmarshalYAML` decodes into a `rawSpec` listing exactly
`Parameters`, `Values`, `Files`, `Dependencies` — its own comment warns
"a field added to Spec alone is silently dropped", and yaml.v3 does not
error on unknown keys. A `spec.local` block would parse to nil with no
error and every `local.yaml` value would fail against an empty catalog.
So this work adds to `internal/template/manifest.go`:

- `Spec.Local *LocalSpec` where `LocalSpec{Fixtures []string}`, repeated
  in `rawSpec` (the whole point of the comment);
- validation in `validate()`: fixture names are non-empty, unique,
  lowercase path-safe tokens;
- a round-trip test asserting a `spec.local.fixtures` block survives
  load — the regression test for the silent-drop failure mode.

`template.yaml` files in the library without a `spec.local` block decode
to nil; the CLI treats a nil or empty catalog on `deploy-component` as a
hard error naming the library ref (a local overlay without a catalog is
a broken release, not a prompt with no choices).

### Workspace root and the state file

Review finding 6: "workspace root" was unstated. Definition: the directory
`selectHost` already searches — the host discovery root, i.e.
`--source-dir` when given, else the current directory, walked per
`ListScaffolds` (which skips `.intropy/` subtrees — no collision). The
state file is `<that root>/.intropy/local.yaml`, beside the host's
`.intropy/scaffold.json`.

Rules:

- A connector with a recorded choice is never re-prompted.
- A connector with no choice prompts (interactive) or errors under
  `--no-input`, listing what's missing.
- Values are validated against the fetched catalog.
- A connector removed from the topology leaves a stale entry; harmless,
  reported as a stderr note (`note: local.yaml binds crm, which the
  topology no longer declares`).
- The file is checked in: the whole team runs the same local topology, and
  CI runs non-interactively.

```yaml
connectors:
  erp-orders: sftp
  crm: http
```

## Values layering for the local render

Re-review finding 4. `int local` has **no `--values` and no `--set`** —
deliberately: every fact the templates need is derived (topology,
scaffold records, local constants, `local.yaml`), and an escape hatch
would let a local render diverge from the team's checked-in state in
ways nobody else can reproduce. Missing required template parameters
prompt through the existing `template.AutoPrompter`, exactly as
`resolveInitValues` drives it; under `--no-input` that prompter returns
nil and the parameter's absence surfaces as a resolve error. So the
`--no-input` failure surface is: unbound connectors (the two-line error
above) plus any template parameter with no default and no derived value.

## Templates work (intropy-templates repo, lands first)

- Add a `local` overlay to `deploy-host` and `deploy-component`. Content
  stays versioned with the templates it derives from, and the
  `INTROPY_TEMPLATES_DIR` integration tests can cover it. A third
  standalone template was considered and rejected: two places describing
  the same Dapr components would drift.
- The `local` overlay carries the fixture catalog: one Dapr binding
  Component skeleton per fixture type, parameterized by connector name,
  pointing at the conventional fixture addresses. `spec.local.fixtures`
  declares the catalog (see above).
- Dev values, not `REPLACE-ME-*` placeholders: unlike `deploy init` (where
  a human fills placeholders before review), local output must apply
  cleanly on first run.
- Skeleton files must honor the `.gitops` emptiness contract (no
  `argocdAppNamespace`/`domain` references in the local overlay).
- `component.yaml` and other repo-metadata files must be declared in
  `spec.files` so the CLI's narrowed filter can exclude them — verify they
  already are; if any are unconditional, move them behind a rule.
- Verify the ApplicationSet's cluster generator cannot produce an
  Application for an `overlays/local/` directory (unregistered cluster ⇒
  no match). Document the result in the template's README.

## CLI implementation (this repo)

New files, mirroring existing seams:

- `internal/deploy/local.go` — `LocalOptions` / `Local` (above). Reuses
  `selectHost`, `discoverTopology`/`TopologyFile`, `newInitModel`,
  `selectComponents`, `template.FetchLibrary`, `renderOne` (with the
  narrowed filter and the local facts), `kustomize.Client.Build`. Adds
  `localFacts` + the root-kustomization writer.
- `internal/deploy/localconfig.go` — load/save/validate
  `.intropy/local.yaml` against the fetched catalog.
- `internal/template/prompt.go` — add `SelectPrompter`.
- `internal/template/manifest.go` — add `Spec.Local` / `LocalSpec`,
  repeat it in `rawSpec`, validate it, round-trip test (see "The
  catalog").
- `cmd/intropy/int_local.go` — cobra wiring.
- `cmd/intropy/flagtext.go` — add `flagUsageNoInput`; convert
  `int_create.go`, `deploy_init.go`, and the new command to it.

Tests (review finding 7 — mirror *both* existing seams):

- Unit: fixture templates served through the `GitHubBaseURL` fetch seam
  (as init_test.go:297 does) + **both** topology seams — package var
  `runGraph` (as init.go:39 establishes) and `LocalOptions.TopologyFile`
  — asserting rendered YAML per binding choice, root-kustomization
  contents (including the pinned image reference shape and the
  host-excluded images list), the untagged-image guard, prompt behavior,
  state-file round-trip, `--no-input` errors, stale-entry notes, and
  host discovery via `selectHost` the way init tests exercise it. Plus
  the manifest.go round-trip test for `spec.local.fixtures`.
- Integration: alongside `localtemplates_test.go`, under the same
  `//go:build integration` tag (rev 1 omitted it), gated on
  `INTROPY_TEMPLATES_DIR` and run with `-count=1`. Renders with the real
  templates, parses the output as YAML, and validates with
  `kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f -` — a second optional tool
  dependency, skipped via a `requireKubectl(t)` helper mirroring
  `requireKustomize`.

Docs:

- `docs/deploy-local.md` — the testing-ladder framing, the boundary table,
  the facts model, the state file, and a pointer to the fixture-contract
  doc. `Long:` stays ≤ 150 words; philosophy lives in the doc.
- `AGENTS.md` — add `local` to the verb taxonomy with the justification
  quoted in "The verb" above.

## Deliberately out of scope

- Building or loading container images.
- Installing anything — cluster, Dapr, fixtures are the scripts' job.
- Cluster introspection: the command never checks whether the cluster
  exists, Dapr is installed, or fixtures are reachable. It renders;
  kubectl applies; a missing cluster fails at apply time with kubectl's
  own error.
- User-defined fixture types (closed catalog).
- Pushing anything, anywhere: no git writes, no branches, no PRs. The only
  file written is `.intropy/local.yaml`.

## Order of work

1. Fixture-contract doc (scripts repo) — names, ports, credentials, the
   `.gitops` emptiness contract, the repo-metadata exclusion list, the
   `image: <component>` convention.
2. `local` overlay + fixture catalog + `spec.local.fixtures`
   (intropy-templates repo) — the CLI work is mostly plumbing against
   this. Includes the ApplicationSet verification.
3. `internal/template/manifest.go` `Spec.Local` +
   `internal/template/prompt.go` `SelectPrompter` + `flagtext.go`
   constant — small, unblocks the rest.
4. `internal/deploy/local.go` + `localconfig.go` + cobra wiring, unit
   tests against fixture templates.
5. Integration test against real templates.
6. `docs/deploy-local.md`, `AGENTS.md` taxonomy entry.

=== README deploy-component ===
# deploy-component

The per-block half of `intropy deploy init`: one workload and one thin overlay
per environment.

Rendered once per topology component into
`domains/<domain>/<system>/<component>/`.

## Workload follows the block kind

An extractor wakes on a schedule, pulls from its source and exits, so it renders
a `CronJob`. Every other block reacts to messages or requests and must stay
resident, so it renders a `Deployment`. `spec.files` picks one and never writes
the other.

This is not an invention: the hand-written manifests in two customer
repositories already run their extractors as CronJobs. The topology's block kind
is what lets the CLI derive it.

The CronJob's schedule is a `REPLACE-ME-CRON-SCHEDULE` placeholder — and its
one and only home. Activation cadence is deployment configuration, so the
topology carries no schedule to copy from; fill it in here and edit it here.

## The image is never pinned here

`spec.values.imageTag` is the literal `unpinned`. `intropy deploy` writes the
digest, and it is the only thing that may. A tag here would let what runs change
without a deployment — which is what got an earlier version of this command
deleted.

`unpinned` rather than `latest` on purpose: it fails to pull loudly, and it reads
correctly in an `ImagePullBackOff`.

## imageNamespace has no safe default

Customers disagree on the path segment between the registry and the image name —
one uses the customer slug, another uses `integrations`. The default is
`integrations`; override it with `--set imageNamespace=<slug>` or a values file.
It must match what CI actually pushes.

## Reserved values

`.env`, `.topology`, `.gitops`, `.component` (this block's derived record) and
`.scaffold` (its `.intropy/scaffold.json` values, or `{}`).

# deploy-host

The system-level half of `intropy deploy init`: the Dapr components a system's
blocks resolve by name, the secret store behind them, and — on a platform
without an external one — the Secret holding the placeholders.

Rendered once per system into `domains/<domain>/<system>/host/`.

## Why these objects live here

A Dapr `Component` is namespace-scoped, and every integration in a customer's
namespace shares it. So exactly one ArgoCD Application may own each one. If each
block owned a copy, N Applications would claim the same `Component/pubsub` and
whichever synced last would win — a live example of that exists in one customer
repository today.

This directory is that single owner. `scopes:` is what limits *use*: it lists
exactly the app-ids the topology says publish to or subscribe from the broker.
Single ownership plus scopes is the correct pair; scopes alone is not.

Its `component.yaml` declares `kind: shared`, which is how `intropy deploy` and
`intropy deploy promote` know to refuse it — there is no image to pin.

## Which files get rendered

`spec.files` decides the *file set*, not just the contents:

| condition | effect |
|---|---|
| `pubsub` | only the matching `base/dapr/pubsub-<broker>.yaml` |
| `secretStore` | only the matching `base/dapr/secretstore-<store>.yaml` |
| `secretStore == kubernetes` | `base/secrets/` at all |
| topology has connectors | `base/bindings/` at all |

`base/kustomization.yaml` references `dapr/pubsub-{{ .pubsub }}.yaml`, so the
list needs no conditional — the file name follows the parameter.

Adding a broker is a new `pubsub-<name>.yaml.tmpl`, a new `enum` value and a new
rule. The CLI is not involved: it passes `platform.pubsub` through from
`deploy.yaml` without knowing what the values mean.

## Everything is identical across environments

The Dapr components live in `base/` and do not vary by environment. What varies
is the *credential*, and a Component reaches that through `secretKeyRef` — so the
same YAML resolves to different values in each environment's namespace. The
overlays are a `namespace:` and a `resources:` line.

One customer repository does vary the broker per overlay (in-memory in dev,
RabbitMQ in prod). That is a deviation, not the convention, and this template
does not reproduce it.

## Reserved values

Beyond the declared parameters, the CLI injects:

- `.env` — the environment being rendered. Only meaningful under `overlays/`; the
  CLI refuses a skeleton where it changes anything else.
- `.topology` — the derived system model: `pubsubs` (with `appIds` for `scopes:`),
  `connectors` (name, directions, appIds — the topology mints names only;
  binding types are owned here, so every connector renders as a REPLACE-ME
  scaffold), `topics`, `components`.
- `.gitops` — `domain`, `system`, `component`, `host`, `registry`,
  `argocdAppNamespace`, `environments`, `platform`.

## Check a change locally

```sh
intropy deploy init --domain sales --topology topology.json --plan
```

Then render what it produced:

```sh
kustomize build domains/sales/<system>/host/overlays/dev
```

apiVersion: dapr.io/v1alpha1
kind: Component
metadata:
  name: {{ .pubsubName }}
spec:
  type: pubsub.rabbitmq
  version: v1
  metadata:
    - name: connectionString
      secretKeyRef:
        name: {{ .secretName }}
        key: rabbitmq-connection
    - name: durable
      value: "true"
    - name: deliveryMode
      value: "2"
# Resolved through the system's secret store, not necessarily a Kubernetes
# Secret: with kubernetes that is the rendered secrets/secrets.yaml, and with
# Key Vault or Vault the key is looked up there instead.
auth:
  secretStore: {{ .system }}-secretstore

# Exactly the app-ids the topology says publish to or subscribe from this
# broker's topics. The Component is namespace-scoped and this directory is its
# only owner, so scopes is what limits who may use it.
scopes:
{{- range .topology.pubsubs }}
{{- range .appIds }}
  - {{ . }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
=== pubsub in-memory ===
# In-memory pub/sub: no broker, and no message leaves the pod. Only correct when
# a single block both publishes and subscribes.
apiVersion: dapr.io/v1alpha1
kind: Component
metadata:
  name: {{ .pubsubName }}
spec:
  type: pubsub.in-memory
  version: v1
scopes:
{{- range .topology.pubsubs }}
{{- range .appIds }}
  - {{ . }}
{{- end }}
{{- end }}
=== secretstore kubernetes ===
# The cluster's own Secret objects. Values come from secrets/secrets.yaml in this
# same directory, which is why that file is only rendered for this store.
apiVersion: dapr.io/v1alpha1
kind: Component
metadata:
  name: {{ .system }}-secretstore
spec:
  type: secretstores.kubernetes
  version: v1
=== secrets ===
# Placeholders, not secrets. Every value here is REPLACE-ME until somebody fills
# it in — which is why nothing in this tree is pushed to the default branch.
#
# If your platform has a real secret manager, point deploy.yaml's
# platform.secretStore at it instead and this file is not rendered at all.
#
# Connector credentials get their entries here when you pick the connectors'
# binding types in base/bindings/bindings.yaml — the topology carries no
# binding types, so no connector keys are pre-rendered.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: {{ .secretName }}
type: Opaque
stringData:
{{- if eq .pubsub "rabbitmq" }}
  rabbitmq-connection: REPLACE-ME-RABBITMQ-CONNECTION-STRING
{{- end }}
{{- if eq .pubsub "servicebus" }}
  servicebus-connection: REPLACE-ME-SERVICEBUS-CONNECTION-STRING
{{- end }}

# intropy-templates

A library of **Intropy templates** — scaffolds rendered into
working projects by the `intropy` CLI (separate repo:
`integrio-intropy/intropy-cli`). This repo contains content, not code: the CLI
is the only renderer.

One engine: Go `text/template` + [sprig](https://masterminds.github.io/sprig/).
One manifest format. One skeleton tree per template.

## Templates

- **`hello-world/`** — minimal example template that exercises the manifest
  and skeleton conventions.
- **`transactional/`** — a transactional integration component template.

Rendered by `intropy deploy init` rather than `intropy int create`, into a
GitOps repository rather than a working project:

- **`deploy-host/`** — a system's shared Dapr components, secret store and
  secret placeholders, owned by one ArgoCD Application.
- **`deploy-component/`** — one block's workload (`CronJob` for an extractor,
  `Deployment` otherwise) and its per-environment overlays.

Those two are the only templates that use `spec.files` to decide which files
exist at all. See [`CLAUDE.md`](./CLAUDE.md) for the rule — and for why no
older template may adopt it yet.

## Template layout

```
<template>/
  template.yaml          required: the intropy.dev/v1 manifest
  skeleton/              required: rendered into the user's --output
    <files…>             `.tmpl` files are templated; everything else is copied
  README.md              optional: author-facing notes
  examples/              optional: test fixtures for local renders
```

Only `template.yaml` and `skeleton/` are seen by the renderer. Anything else at
the template root is for the author, not the scaffolded project.

## Rendering locally

```bash
intropy int create hello-world -o /tmp/hello-out \
    -f hello-world/examples/minimal.yaml --version main
```

Pass `--version main` while there is no release yet. Once releases exist, the
default `--version` resolves to the latest tag.

## Conventions

See [`CLAUDE.md`](./CLAUDE.md) for the full manifest schema and skeleton
conventions. In short:

- File contents are templated only when the filename ends in `.tmpl` (the
  suffix is stripped on output). Path segments are always templated.
- Reference parameters and derived values with `{{ .paramName }}`.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code when working in this repository.

## What this repo is

A library of **Intropy templates**. Each template is a scaffold
rendered into a working project by the `intropy` CLI (separate repo:
`integrio-intropy/intropy-cli`). The CLI is the only renderer; this repo
contains content, not code.

The model is intentionally narrow: one engine (Go `text/template` + sprig),
one manifest format, one source of truth per template.

## Repository layout

```
<template>/
  template.yaml          # required: the intropy.dev/v1 manifest
  skeleton/              # required: rendered into the user's --output
    <files…>             # `.tmpl` files are templated; everything else is copied
  README.md              # optional: author-facing — what this template produces
  examples/              # optional: test fixtures for local renders
    minimal.yaml
    full.yaml
```

Rules:

- The CLI selects a template via positional argument:
  `intropy int create hello-world -o ./out`.
- Only `<template>/template.yaml` is parsed; only `<template>/skeleton/` is
  walked by the renderer.
- Anything else at the template root (README, examples, CHANGELOG, ADRs) is
  invisible to the renderer — it's for the template author, not the
  scaffolded project.
- There is **no shared content between templates**. No repo-level
  `skeletons/` dir, no cross-template includes. If two templates need the
  same file, duplicate it. (Composition happens at the *output* level:
  a template may declare whole sibling templates under `spec.dependencies`
  — see below — but never share skeleton files with them.)

## Manifest schema (`<template>/template.yaml`)

```yaml
apiVersion: intropy.dev/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: <kebab-case>           # convention: match the directory name
  title: <Title Case>
  description: <one sentence>
  tags: [example, go, http]
  labels:                      # two intropy.dev/* keys are load-bearing (see below)
    intropy.io/template-level: example
    intropy.dev/block-kind: extractor   # extractor | loader | aggregator | transactional-integration
    intropy.dev/data-flow: "in"         # in | out | both | internal
spec:
  parameters:                  # raw JSON Schema; type must be "object"
    type: object
    required: [name]
    properties:
      name:
        type: string
        title: Service name
        description: Lowercase kebab-case identifier.
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      port:
        type: integer
        default: 8080
  values:                      # optional; derived values rendered via Go template + sprig
    module: 'github.com/example/{{ .name }}'
  dependencies:                # optional; sibling templates scaffolded when missing
    - template: shared-contracts  # directory name in this repo
      output: '{{ .contracts }}'  # Go template; single path segment (conventionally "Contracts")
      values:                  # Go templates over this template's resolved values
        name: '{{ .contracts }}'
```

Notes:

content.text:
- **`spec.parameters` is plain JSON Schema.** Types: `string`, `boolean`,
  `integer`, `number`. Supported attributes: `title`, `description`, `pattern`,
  `enum`, `default`. The same schema validates CLI inputs and drives the
  Backstage form when a Template entity references this template.
- **Parameter declaration order matters** for human display. Keep the YAML
  order intentional.
- **`spec.values` derives string values from parameters.** Each entry is a Go
  template (with sprig) rendered against the resolved parameters. Use for
  composite values needed in multiple skeleton files (e.g. a module path).
  Output is always a string. Don't chain entries — map iteration order
  is non-deterministic.
- **Two labels are load-bearing.** The CLI reads `intropy.dev/block-kind`
  (`extractor` | `loader` | `aggregator` | `transactional-integration`) and
  `intropy.dev/data-flow` (`in` | `out` | `both` | `internal`) at render time
  and records them in the scaffolded project's `.intropy/scaffold.json`, which
  `intropy sys create` later assembles into the system declaration. Templates
  that are a system block must declare both. Everything else under `labels`
  is free-form.
- **`spec.dependencies` composes whole templates at the output level.** Each
  entry names a sibling template in this repo, an `output` (a Go template
  that must render to a single path segment — the dependency is created as a
  direct sibling of the component's output directory), and a `values` map
  (Go templates rendered against the declaring template's resolved values).
  The CLI renders dependencies from the same fetched tag right after the
  component render. Idempotency: a target directory whose
  `.intropy/scaffold.json` names the same template is **skipped silently**
  (drift in values only warns); a missing or empty directory is rendered; a
  foreign scaffold record or an unmanaged non-empty directory is an error.
  `--force` never propagates to dependencies. The component's scaffold
  record lists every declared dependency under `dependsOn`.
  Authoring rules:
  - A dependency render never prompts — the `values` map plus the dependency
    template's own defaults must cover all its required parameters.
  - Shared-support templates (like `shared-contracts`) declare
    `intropy.dev/template-role: shared-library` and **no**
    `intropy.dev/block-kind` / `data-flow` labels; the role is recorded in
    scaffold.json so system assembly can tell them apart from blocks.
  - A skeleton may reference its declared dependencies (e.g. a
    `ProjectReference` to `../../<dep>/…`) — the mechanism guarantees the
    sibling exists. The system-host skeleton never references the workspace's
    shared contracts project; `intropy sys create` discovers it by its
    scaffold record and inserts that reference itself.
- **`spec.files` decides which files exist at all**, where `spec.parameters`
  only decides what is in them. Each entry is a `path` glob relative to
  `skeleton/` plus a `when` — a Go template (sprig available) rendered against
  the resolved values. Any result other than `""`, `"false"` or `"0"` includes
  the match.

  ```yaml
  files:
    - path: base/dapr/pubsub-servicebus.yaml.tmpl
      when: '{{ eq .pubsub "servicebus" }}'
    - path: base/dapr/pubsub-rabbitmq.yaml.tmpl
      when: '{{ eq .pubsub "rabbitmq" }}'
    - path: base/secrets/**
      when: '{{ eq .secretStore "kubernetes" }}'
  ```

  Rules:
  - **The first matching rule decides**, so a specific rule can override a
    broader one placed after it. A path no rule matches is **included** — which
    is why every template written before this field existed renders unchanged.
  - **Paths match the source**, `.tmpl` suffix included. A rule that decides on
    values cannot depend on a path those values produce, so a
    `{{ .name }}/` segment is only reachable via a glob.
  - **A trailing `/**` matches the directory and everything under it**, and
    prunes the subtree *before* its contents are parsed. So a skeleton may carry
    a file that is not even a valid template for the values in play.
  - `*` does not cross a `/`, so `dapr/*.yaml` cannot silently prune
    `dapr/nested/x.yaml`.
  - `when` is required and parsed at load time: a syntax error fails
    immediately rather than part way through a render. `missingkey=error`
    applies, so a typo'd value name is a loud error, not a silent skip.
  - **Prefer a value-derived filename over a conditional list.** If the rendered
    file is named after the parameter that selected it
    (`pubsub-{{ .pubsub }}.yaml`), a `kustomization.yaml` referencing it needs
    no conditional at all.

  ⚠️ **Do not add `spec.files` to a pre-existing template until the CLI floor
  moves.** The CLI parses manifests without rejecting unknown fields, so an
  older CLI reading a template that uses `spec.files` silently **ignores the
  filter and renders every file** — a wrong answer with no error. New templates
  fetched only by a new command (`deploy-host`, `deploy-component`) are safe
  because no old CLI ever fetches them.

- **No `spec.steps`**, no `spec.owner`, no `nextSteps`. The model is
  intentionally narrow: a manifest declares parameters and the skeleton tree
  describes what gets written.

## Skeleton conventions (`<template>/skeleton/`)

- **File contents are templated only if the filename ends in `.tmpl`.** The
  `.tmpl` suffix is stripped on output (`README.md.tmpl` → `README.md`).
- **Filenames and directory names are templated** with the same `{{ .param }}`
  syntax as file contents (e.g. `src/{{ .name }}.csproj`). The `.tmpl` suffix
  only governs whether *file contents* are rendered; path segments are always
  templated.
- **Use `{{ .paramName }}` to reference parameters and derived values.** The
  data context is a flat map containing parameters + `spec.values` entries.
- **Sprig is available.** `upper`, `lower`, `title`, `kebabcase`,
  `snakecase`, `replace`, `default`, `trim`, `len`, `get`, `dict`. Full list:
  https://masterminds.github.io/sprig/ .
- **Missing keys are a hard error.** The renderer runs with
  `missingkey=error`. Typos like `{{ .Name }}` (wrong case) fail the render
  with a clear message — they don't silently produce empty strings.
- **Sprig functions with side effects exist** (`env`, `now`, `uuidv4`,
  `getHostByName`). Don't use them — they break the "same inputs → same
  output" reproducibility guarantee.

Example skeleton file `skeleton/README.md.tmpl`:

```markdown
# {{ .name }}

Generated from the `{{ .name }}` template.

Module: `{{ .module }}`
```

## The local overlay

`overlays/local/` is rendered by `intropy int local`, not `deploy init`: a
one-off render for the local development cluster, piped straight to
`kubectl apply -f -`. It differs from the environment overlays in three ways.

**The image reference is pinned to a bare name.** `deployment.yaml` and
`cronjob-local.yaml` render `image: {{ .name }}` — no registry prefix, no
tag — exactly when `.env` is `local`. `int local` writes a root kustomization
whose `images[]` entries rewrite that reference to `<name>:dev`, the tag the
k3s setup scripts build and load component images under. kustomize matches
`images[]` on the exact rendered string and **silently ignores a miss**, so
the bare-name shape is part of the contract; the CLI also fails the render if
any built Deployment image has no tag, as a second net.

**The fixture bindings live here.** `overlays/local/fixtures/` carries one
Dapr binding skeleton per fixture type — the closed catalog declared in
`spec.local.fixtures` (`sftp`, `smb`, `http`, `file`). Each file renders one
`Component` per topology connector whose recorded binding in the workspace's
`.intropy/local.yaml` names that fixture, and nothing when none do; the CLI
fails the render if every catalog file comes out empty, because a bindingless
local overlay is a template release bug, not a system state. `int local`
prompts for and validates the bindings, so the values are always catalog
members.

**Dev values, not placeholders.** Every fixture skeleton points at the
conventional fixture server the k3s setup scripts always install —
`sftp.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:22` (`intropy`/`intropy`),
`smb.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:445`, `http.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:8080`
(wiremock-style stub), and `/data/<connector>` in the component's own
container for `file`. That fixture contract — namespace, service names,
ports, credentials, the bare image reference above — is shared with the k3s
setup scripts and is the only coupling between the two; the rendered
manifests are otherwise generic and apply to any cluster with Dapr and the
fixtures installed. Local output must apply cleanly on first run, so nothing
under `overlays/local/` renders a `REPLACE-ME-*` value.

The overlay renders no namespace and no image override of its own: the CLI's
root kustomization sets both, so the same overlay serves any `--namespace`
and any `--image` override without re-rendering.

### Why a connector's binding lives with the component

`deploy init` renders bindings on the host because a customer cluster
resolves their credentials through the system's secret store, which the host
owns. The local cluster needs no secret store — fixture credentials are
public dev values — and the catalog files *can* live on the host (they render
identically there). They live here anyway: a connector is scoped to exactly
the app-ids that use it, and keeping the binding beside the block that
resolves it keeps one component's fixture choices out of every other
component's render. The host's `base/bindings/bindings.yaml` is not rendered
locally — the CLI renders only the local overlay, and only this overlay
references fixture files.

### ApplicationSet safety

If this rendered tree ever lands in a GitOps repository, `overlays/local/`
must not produce an ArgoCD Application. It cannot: the ApplicationSet that
fans overlays out to clusters generates from its *cluster* generator, which
matches only clusters registered in ArgoCD — the local development cluster
never is — so a `local` overlay resolves to no cluster and no Application.
There is no path segment in the generator to match on.

## Reserved values

`.env`, `.topology`, `.gitops`, `.component` (this block's derived record),
`.scaffold` (its `.intropy/scaffold.json` values, or `{}`) and — local
renders only — `.local`, the decided bindings: `.local.bindings` maps
connector name to fixture name.

package main

// int local renders a system's manifests for the local development cluster
// to stdout. Everything non-trivial — topology discovery, the connector
// prompt, rendering, the kustomize build — lives in internal/deploy.Local;
// this file is flag plumbing and the call.
type localFlags struct {
	namespace       string
	images          []string
	templateVersion string
	templateRepo    string
	noInput         bool
}

var intLocalFlags localFlags

var intLocalCmd = &cobra.Command{
	Use:   "local <system>",
	Short: "Render a system's manifests for the local development cluster",
	Long: "Render deployable manifests for the local development cluster to stdout, for piping to kubectl: " +
		"`intropy int local <system> | kubectl apply -f -`.\n\n" +
		"The topology comes from the system host, exactly as deploy init reads it. Each connector needs a " +
		"fixture binding; the command asks once per connector and records the answers in .intropy/local.yaml, " +
		"checked in so the team renders the same thing. The fixture catalog comes from the fetched template " +
		"library release.\n\n" +
		"Component images render as <component>:dev. --image overrides that: --image <component>=<name:tag> " +
		"for one component, --image :<tag> for all.\n\n" +
		"The command never inspects the cluster and writes nothing but the state file; a missing cluster " +
		"fails at apply time with kubectl's own error. See docs/deploy-local.md for the boundary between this " +
		"command, the k3s scripts and the template overlays.",
	Args: cobra.ExactArgs(1),
	RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
		owner, repo, err := resolveTemplateRepo(intLocalFlags.templateRepo)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}

		ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(cmd.Context(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
		defer cancel()

		return deploy.Local(ctx, deploy.LocalOptions{
			System:          args[0],
			Namespace:       intLocalFlags.namespace,
			Images:          intLocalFlags.images,
			NoInput:         intLocalFlags.noInput,
			TemplateVersion: intLocalFlags.templateVersion,
			UserAgent:       "intropy-cli/" + version,
			Owner:           owner,
			Repo:            repo,
			Stdin:           cmd.InOrStdin(),
			Stdout:          cmd.OutOrStdout(),
			Stderr:          cmd.ErrOrStderr(),
		})
	},
}

func init() {
	f := intLocalCmd.Flags()
	f.StringVar(&intLocalFlags.namespace, "namespace", "", "target namespace in the emitted manifests (default: the system name)")
	f.StringArrayVar(&intLocalFlags.images, "image", nil, "image override: <component>=<name:tag> for one component, :<tag> for all (repeatable)")
	f.StringVar(&intLocalFlags.templateVersion, "template-version", "", flagUsageTemplateVer)
	f.StringVar(&intLocalFlags.templateRepo, "template-repo", "", flagUsageTemplateRepo)
	f.BoolVar(&intLocalFlags.noInput, "no-input", false, flagUsageNoInput)
	intCmd.AddCommand(intLocalCmd)
}

Both fixes are committed. Here's the complete picture:

## Why `bindings.sftp` wasn't rendered — two compounding bugs

**Bug 1 (CLI, `internal/deploy/local.go`).** `localFileRules` rewrote every `spec.files` rule's `when` to the prose string `"repo metadata; a local render emits manifests only"`, intending an always-false exclusion. But the filter's `truthy()` treats any non-empty string that isn't `""`/`"false"`/`"0"` as **true** — so every conditional file was *included* instead of excluded.

**Bug 2 (walk-order collision).** With everything included, both `overlays/local/kustomization.yaml.tmpl` and `overlays/{{ .env }}/kustomization.yaml.tmpl` rendered to `overlays/local/kustomization.yaml`. Go's `filepath.WalkDir` walks `local/` before `{{ .env }}/` (`l` < `{` byte-wise), so the thin environment overlay was written **last**, silently overwriting the fixture-carrying one. The fixture files rendered fine but nothing referenced them — and the host's REPLACE-ME binding scaffold is what reached your output.

## Fixes

**CLI** (`f41f7899` on `feature/int-local`): `localFileRules` now prepends an exclusion for repo metadata (`component.yaml`) with a literal `"false"` condition, and **keeps** the template's real rules. With the local facts seeded (`pubsub: redis`, workload, `secretStore: kubernetes`), those rules select exactly the right variants — and keep the generic overlay from shadowing the local one.

**Templates** (`5ffd049` on `feature/local-overlay`):
- Generic `overlays/{{ .env }}/` excluded for the local environment via `spec.files`; deploy-host ships a dedicated namespaceless `overlays/local/` skeleton. `local` is now a reserved environment name.
- Host REPLACE-ME bindings scaffold excluded for local (fixtures are the only local binding owner) — was colliding with every fixture Component.
- Each fixture skeleton now emits a connector only in the component whose appId is **first** in the connector's scopes — was rendering the same Component once per component, which kustomize rejects as a duplicate.

Verified end-to-end: `erp: sftp` in `.intropy/local.yaml` now produces exactly one `type: bindings.sftp` Component with `sftp.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:22`, no REPLACE-ME anywhere, passes `kubectl apply --dry-run=client`, and all unit + integration suites are green.
